blocks.heading: Compare the Practical Paths
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Photography genres, ranked by how far they can scale

rows: AI-era commercial production (your photos plus editing, retouching and AI-made variations for brands)
Scalable

Sold directly to brands and sellers who need many images fast. One skilled person can serve many clients, and you can later add a small team. The edge is that you can shoot the real product and also make the extra variations that tools now make cheap.
Wedding and event photography (often with video)
Scalable with a business layer
Real demand, because a wedding happens once and cannot be redone. Income is capped by your own dates until you build a studio with second shooters, editors and packages.
Drone, real estate and architecture photography
Scalable with a business layer
Brokers, builders and hotels need repeat shoots. A drone licence and local contacts create a barrier. Repeat work for the same few clients is the business layer.
Product and e-commerce photography
Scalable with a business layer

Brands need steady images, which suits monthly retainers. Plain catalogue shots are the part tools are taking first, so the business layer is styling, speed and brand consistency, not one-off white-background shots.
Fashion and portrait photography
Not so scalable

Crowded, and it has two hard stages: first get noticed by labels, agencies or private clients, then become a name that is booked at higher rates. Plain catalogue work is also exposed to AI models. A studio with a creative-direction offer is the only business layer.
Photojournalism and newsroom photography
Not so scalable
Staff photo jobs have shrunk and many photographers have moved to freelance. Mostly an employer route, so the sales layer matters for the freelance move after it.

blocks.heading: What AI Changes in Each Genre
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: What AI changes in each genre
rows: Wildlife and Travel
Field Craft, Patience and a Trusted Name.
Wildlife and Travel
Field Craft, Patience and a Trusted Name.
Product and e-commerce
High
Amazon's own seller blog describes a tool that turns basic product photos into lifestyle images. Sellers can now make several variations from one photo.
Fashion catalogue
High for plain catalogue
A December 2025 industry post names high-volume catalogue shoots and basic e-commerce listings as the most exposed to AI models. Its cost claims are unsourced.
Stock
High
The US labour-data office says stock work may be partly replaced by AI images, and big libraries now sell AI-made images.
Wedding and event
Low risk of replacement, high change in workflow
Tools that sort and edit a full wedding in minutes are sold to photographers. The claims come from the tool makers, so test them on your own files. Expect clients to ask for faster delivery.
Photojournalism
Low from AI, high from shrinking newsrooms
Photographers quoted by Newslaundry in 2023 blamed phone cameras and shrinking space for photographs, not AI, for the decline.
Wildlife and travel
Low for the real shot
Our judgement: fake images will make people who buy prints and trips ask who really took the picture.
Product and e-commerce
Accurate real-product shots, reflections, texture, and styling that tools handle badly. Vendors admit saree drape is hard to render.
Fashion catalogue
Luxury, editorial and emotion-led campaigns still use real people. A direction and styling skill keeps you in the room.
Stock
Very little. Genuine local, editorial and documentary pictures that tools cannot invent are the narrow gap.
Wedding and event
Being there. Reading a room, handling elders, catching a once-only moment, and keeping the family calm.
Photojournalism
Access, trust and being on the ground. Verified pictures matter more as fake images spread.

blocks.heading: Who Should Skip Photography As a Career
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Who should skip photography as a career

rows: You need a fixed salary every month from the first year
Self-employed photography pays by booked dates. Studio jobs exist but listed fresher pay is low. Plan a second income while you build.
You dislike talking to clients and families
Most of the job is people: briefs, changes, late payment, and handling relatives at events. The camera is the smaller part.
You love shooting but hate editing and admin
Culling, editing, delivery, invoices and follow-up often take more hours than shooting.
You plan to take a loan for gear before any paid job
A loan turns a slow start into a debt problem. Rent first and buy when jobs pay for it.
Your dream is only wildlife or only fashion
These are the most crowded and the slowest to pay. Keep a second genre that pays while you build the dream.
You think AI makes this a safe, easy field now or a dead field now
Both are wrong. Some genres lose work to AI fast and others change slowly. Check your genre in the AI table above.
